mission_03: Mahalanobis distance extends outlier detection to the multivariate setting by accounting for correlations between features. Unlike univariate methods that examine each feature independently, Mahalanobis distance measures how far a point is from the center of the distribution in units that account for the shape and orientation of the data cloud. A point may appear normal in each individual dimension but be a multivariate outlier due to an unusual combination of values. The squared Mahalanobis distance follows a chi-squared distribution with degrees of freedom equal to the number of features, providing a principled statistical threshold. This method is essential for detecting anomalies in correlated feature spaces and is widely used in quality control, fraud detection, and multivariate process monitoring.
